```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(ermeeth2)
library(dplyr)
```

The dictionary of `ermeeth2` names the variables of ThreeME in plots and tables. It is far from finished: most variables have a long description and no short label, and the French has not been reviewed. This guide says **which file to change** for each kind of improvement, and how to rebuild the dictionary afterwards.

It is about the dictionary shipped with the package, shared by everyone. To name variables for one project only, no change to the package is needed: see [Labels and dictionaries](https://www.ofce.fr/threeme/reference/qmd_simulations/labels_dictionary.html).

## Where things stand

```{r}
#| label: status
#| echo: false
d <- threeme_dictionary()
status <- data.frame(
  What = c("Variables in the dictionary",
           "with a short label in English",
           "with a short label in French",
           "whose full English label fits in 25 characters",
           "with a unit",
           "with a group"),
  Variables = c(nrow(d), sum(!is.na(d$label_short_en)), sum(!is.na(d$label_short_fr)),
                sum(nchar(d$label_en) <= 25, na.rm = TRUE), sum(!is.na(d$unit)), sum(!is.na(d$group)))
)
knitr::kable(status)
```

A table shows the short label of a variable. Without one, it falls back on the full label, and on the code when that label is longer than 25 characters. So the most useful thing to add is **short labels**.

## The three files

Everything is in the `data-raw/` folder of the `ermeeth2` repository.

| File | What it holds | Edit it? |
|---|---|---|
| `dictionary.csv` | What people wrote: short labels, units, groups, corrected labels. One line per variable. | **Yes. This is the main one.** |
| `dictionary_survey_fr.csv` | The French translation of each description found in the model, one pair per line. | Yes, to correct a translation. |
| `dictionary_survey.csv` | What the `.mdl` files of the model say about each variable. | **No**: it is written by a script, and a change made by hand is lost at the next run. |

The dictionary of the package is built from them, in this order: the survey first, then `dictionary.csv` on top of it, **cell by cell**. A line of `dictionary.csv` only has to hold what it adds or corrects; whatever it leaves empty comes from the survey.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  mdl["<b>.mdl files</b> of ThreeME_V4<br/>the ##! line above an equation"] -->|dictionary_survey.R| survey["dictionary_survey.csv<br/><i>generated</i>"]
  fr["<b>dictionary_survey_fr.csv</b><br/>French translations"] -->|dictionary_survey.R| survey
  survey -->|dictionary.R| pkg["dictionary of the package"]
  csv["<b>dictionary.csv</b><br/>written by hand, wins"] -->|dictionary.R| pkg
```

The three places in bold are where a person writes.

## Which file for which change

| I want to | Change |
|---|---|
| give a variable a short label | `dictionary.csv` |
| set its unit, its group, how it is usually read | `dictionary.csv` |
| replace a full label that reads badly | `dictionary.csv` |
| describe a variable that is not in the model (an indicator computed in a report) | `dictionary.csv` |
| correct a French translation | `dictionary_survey_fr.csv` |
| describe a variable that has no description at all | the `##!` line of its equation, in the `.mdl` file |
| correct the English description of an equation | the `##!` line of its equation, in the `.mdl` file |

## Editing `dictionary.csv`

### The columns

| Column | Content | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `code` | root code of the variable, in upper case, without sector or commodity | `PCH` |
| `label_en`, `label_fr` | full label | `Consumption price` |
| `label_short_en`, `label_short_fr` | short label, for table rows: aim for 15 characters or fewer | `Cons. price` |
| `unit` | unit of the level | `M€`, `index`, `%` |
| `default_transformation` | how the variable is usually read | `reldiff` |
| `group` | group of the variable in a table | `Prices` |
| `indexed_by` | `sector`, `commodity`, `sector,commodity`, or empty | `commodity` |
| `definition_en`, `definition_fr` | one sentence of definition | |

Only `code` is compulsory. Leave a cell empty when you have nothing to say: the survey fills in the full labels and `indexed_by` on its own.

`default_transformation` must be one of these:

```{r}
#| label: transformations
#| echo: false
tr <- threeme_transformations()
knitr::kable(data.frame(Value = names(tr),
                        Meaning = vapply(tr, function(x) x$label, character(1)),
                        row.names = NULL))
```

Use `ppdiff` for rates and shares (unemployment rate, saving rate), `diff` for head counts read in absolute terms, `reldiff` for the rest.

### Adding a short label

The variable `YQ` has a full label from the model, "Domestic production, expressed at basic price", and no short one. Add a line holding its code and the two short labels, and nothing else:

```csv
"code","label_en","label_fr","label_short_en","label_short_fr","unit","default_transformation","group","indexed_by","definition_en","definition_fr"
"YQ",,,"Dom. production","Production dom.",,,,,,
```

Its full labels still come from the model. If the line already exists, fill in the two cells.

### Describing a variable fully

```csv
"UNR","Unemployment rate (in %)","Taux de chômage (en %)","Unempl. rate","Taux de chômage","%","ppdiff","Labour market",,"Unemployed as a share of the labour force.","Chômeurs rapportés à la population active."
```

### Rules of the file

- One line per code, in upper case. The build stops if a code appears twice.
- The code is the **root**: `CH`, not `CH_CIND`. A sectoral variable takes the label of its root.
- Keep the quotes around the text, and the commas: a label that contains a comma must be inside quotes.
- Save as UTF-8, so that accents survive. A spreadsheet is fine for editing if it exports a plain CSV with commas; check the result in a text editor before committing.

## Correcting a French translation

`dictionary_survey_fr.csv` pairs each English description with its French version:

```csv
"label_long_en","label_long_fr"
"Capacity utilization ratio of the sector s","Taux d'utilisation des capacités du secteur s"
```

Change the second column. **Do not touch the first**: it is the key that ties the translation to the description of the model, character for character.

The translations use a fixed vocabulary, worth keeping consistent:

| English | French |
|---|---|
| commodity c | produit c |
| sector s | secteur s |
| notional | notionnel |
| domestically produced / imported | domestique / importé |
| market price / basic price | prix de marché / prix de base |
| households / Government | ménages / administrations publiques |
| intermediate consumption | consommation intermédiaire |
| change in inventories | variation de stocks |
| toe | tep |

To correct the label of one of the few dozen variables described by hand, change `label_fr` in `dictionary.csv` instead: that file wins.

## Describing a variable in the model

The description of a variable is the `##!` line written just above its equation, in the `.mdl` files of `ThreeME_V4` (`src/model/threeme/`). An exogenous variable is described the same way in `exogenous.mdl`.

```
##! Market price of the intermediate consumption of commodity $c$
PCI[c] * CI[c]   = PCID[c] * CID[c] + PCIM[c] * CIM[c]                if CI[c]  <> 0
```

This is the best place to describe a variable, because the same line also feeds the documentation of the equations. Write it in English, as a noun phrase, starting with a capital letter and without a final full stop.

Two things follow from a change there:

- the survey has to be run again (next section), with `ThreeME_V4` up to date next to `ermeeth2`;
- a description that is new or reworded has no French yet. Add a line for it in `dictionary_survey_fr.csv`, with the English text exactly as the survey reports it in `dictionary_survey.csv` (column `label_long_en`).

## Rebuilding the dictionary

In the `ermeeth2` project, with the package loaded:

```r
pkgload::load_all()

## only if a .mdl file or dictionary_survey_fr.csv changed
source("data-raw/dictionary_survey.R")

## always
source("data-raw/dictionary.R")
```

The first script reads the `.mdl` files in `../ThreeME_V4/src/model/threeme`: the two repositories must sit side by side. It ends by saying how many variables have an English and a French label; if the French count is lower, some descriptions are missing from `dictionary_survey_fr.csv`.

The second writes `data/threeme_dictionary_data.rda`, the dictionary the package ships. It stops if a code is duplicated, or if a `default_transformation` or an `indexed_by` is not one of the values allowed.

### Checking the result

```r
pkgload::load_all()

dict_label(c("YQ", "UNR"))                              # the labels you changed
dict_label(c("YQ", "UNR"), lang = "fr", short = TRUE)

devtools::test(filter = "dictionary|simple_plot|table_3me")
```

Then look at a real table: a label that reads well in a list can still be too wide in a table.

```r
table_3me(data_full, c("GDP", "YQ", "UNR"), lang = "fr")
```

### Sharing it

1. Bump the version in `DESCRIPTION` and add a line to `NEWS.md`.
2. Commit the files you edited **and** the files the scripts rewrote: `data-raw/dictionary_survey.csv` and `data/threeme_dictionary_data.rda`.
3. Open a pull request on [ThreeME-org/ermeeth2](https://github.com/ThreeME-org/ermeeth2). A CSV shows line by line what changed, which is what makes a label easy to review.

Not set up to do this? Open an [issue](https://github.com/ThreeME-org/ermeeth2/issues) with the code of the variable and the label you propose, or send the lines to the ThreeME team.

## Where to start

The variables below are in the standard tables and reports, or in the basic model, and have a full label too long to show in a table and no short one. Each needs one line in `dictionary.csv`.

```{r}
#| label: todo
#| echo: false
todo <- d |>
  filter(is.na(label_short_en), nchar(label_en) > 25) |>
  mutate(length = nchar(label_en)) |>
  arrange(nchar(code), code) |>
  select(Code = code, `Full label` = label_en) |>
  head(40)
knitr::kable(todo)
```

These are the 40 shortest codes, which tend to be the most used; `r sum(is.na(d$label_short_en) & nchar(d$label_en) > 25, na.rm = TRUE)` variables are in this situation in all. The complete list, with a search box, is on the [ThreeME variables](variables_dictionary.html) page.
